subtitle: Where Mandu Wrote Its Hunger for Power in Ink and Spice

panels.shot: wide, slightly low-angle view of a twilight terrace above Mandu, with Ghiyas-ud-din Khalji seated amid dishes and scrolls, the Nimatnama manuscript open before him
panels.action: Ghiyas-ud-din Khalji sits cross-legged on a carved stone terrace above Mandu’s plateau, surrounded by platters, perfumes and attendants, while a richly painted manuscript lies open on a low stand beside him as scribes and painters wait at the edge of the lamplight.

dialogue.text: In a hilltop court famed for pleasure, a sultan’s love of feasts became a painted book of recipes and remedies—the Nimatnama—where food, fragrance and desire turned into a script of power.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ियों की सुख-सभा में, एक सुल्तान की दावत‑दीवानगी से बनी तस्वीरों वाली नुस्ख़ों की किताब – निमत्नामा – जहाँ खाना, ख़ुशबू और चाहत, ताक़त की ज़ुबान बन गए।

panels.shot: aerial bird’s-eye over Mandu’s fortified plateau, showing palaces, tanks and the surrounding Malwa landscape at dawn
panels.action: From high above, the walled plateau of Mandu stretches across the Malwa horizon, its palaces, mosques and water tanks catching the first light of dawn amid fields and forests below.

dialogue.text: Late in the fifteenth century, the hill city of Mandu watched the Deccan and the Gangetic plains from its stone crown, a Malwa court between Rajput domains, Bahmani power and Delhi’s fading reach.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी के आख़िर में, पत्थर के ताज जैसी पहाड़ी नगरी मांडू, राजपूत इलाकों, बहमनी ताक़त और ढलती दिल्ली के बीच बैठी, दक्कन और गंगा के मैदान ताकती थी।

panels.shot: interior wide of the Mandu audience hall, with Ghiyas-ud-din on the throne but slightly turned away from martial displays toward entertainers and food-bearers
panels.action: In the audience hall, Ghiyas-ud-din Khalji sits on a low throne under intricate arches while soldiers and petitioners stand to one side, yet his gaze drifts instead toward musicians, serving women and trays of delicacies carried in by attendants.

dialogue.text: Persian chronicler Firishta would later remember Ghiyas-ud-din Khalji as a ruler who stepped back from conquest, turning his court toward music, women, perfumes and elaborate feasts.

i18n.hi: फ़ारसी इतिहासकार फिरिश्ता ने ग़ियास-उद-दीन खिलजी को एक ऐसे बादशाह की तरह लिखा, जिसने फ़तह से क़दम खींच कर दरबार को राग, रसोई, औरतों, अतर और मेहमाननवाज़ी की तरफ़ मोड़ दिया।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Ghiyas-ud-din in private, in semi-profile, watching as a confection is prepared on a low brazier
panels.action: In a smaller chamber, Ghiyas-ud-din leans forward with quiet curiosity as cooks kneel over a brazier, pouring syrup over a mound of nuts and seeds while an attendant wafts away the steam with a palm fan.

dialogue.text: Where earlier sultans of Malwa had forged their authority in campaigns, Ghiyas-ud-din cultivated another language of rule—hospitality, abundance and the careful tending of the body and its pleasures.

i18n.hi: जहाँ पुराने मालवा सुल्तान जंगों से रुआब बनाते थे, ग़ियास-उद-दीन ने हुकूमत की दूसरी ज़ुबान अपनाई – मेहमाननवाज़ी, नेमतों की रौनक और जिस्म की नाज़ुक देखभाल।

panels.shot: close interior shot of a scribe’s hand beginning to write on a fresh folio, next to pigment shells and brushes
panels.action: A scribe’s hand dips a reed pen into ink and draws the first elegant Persian letters on a fresh burnished page, while shallow dishes of lapis, vermilion and gold pigments sit waiting beside slender brushes.

dialogue.text: Out of this courtly world, sometime between about 1495 and 1505, a project took shape: scribes and painters began to gather recipes and remedies into a single illustrated manuscript.

i18n.hi: इसी दरबारी दुनिया में, करीब 1495 से 1505 के बीच, एक काम शुरू हुआ: कातिबों और नक़्क़ाशों ने नुस्ख़े और नुस्ख़ा‑एइलाज एक ही रंगीन मज़मूए में जुटाने शुरू किए।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder view of the scribe’s page, showing the title line naming the work for Nasir al-Din Shah, unfinished illumination around it
panels.action: From behind the scribe, the page reveals a heading in neat Persian script naming the book for Nasir al-Din Shah, while a pale framework of marginal illumination waits to be filled with colour and gold.

dialogue.text: Its title, Nimatnama-i-Nasiruddin-Shahi, would link it to Ghiyas-ud-din’s successor Nasir Shah, reminding us that this was not the private notebook of one man, but a courtly enterprise spanning two reigns.

i18n.hi: उसका नाम ‘निमत्नामा‑ए नासिरुद्दीन शाही’ उसे ग़ियास के बाद के सुल्तान नासिर शाह से जोड़ता है, याद दिलाते हुए कि ये किसी एक शख़्स की निजी डायरी नहीं, दो दौरों में फैला दरबारी प्रोजेक्ट था।

panels.shot: wide shot of a workshop room with multiple artisans: a scribe writing, a painter colouring a miniature, another burnishing paper
panels.action: In a airy workshop, a scribe bends over a text folio, a painter sits cross-legged applying colour to a miniature of diners, and another artisan polishes a sheet with a smooth stone as finished pages dry on shelves.

dialogue.text: Within the palace, a kitabkhana of artisans carried the work: scribes shaping each line, painters composing scenes, paper-burnishers and binders assembling a single object that blended word, image and taste.

i18n.hi: महल के अंदर किताबख़ाना इस काम पर लगा था: कातिब हर लाइन सँवारते, नक़्क़ाश मंज़र बनाते, काग़ज़ मलने वाले और जिल्दसाज़, लफ़्ज़, तस्वीर और ज़ायके को एक ही जिस्म में जोड़ते।

panels.shot: tight shot on a painted miniature in progress, showing a platter of sweets and a seated figure in Indo-Persian garments against a patterned backdrop
panels.action: A painter’s hand hovers over a small folio where a scene unfolds: a figure in a turbaned cap and local garments sits on a low platform while attendants present a circular platter of sweets set against a patterned screen.

dialogue.text: The images reveal a style on the cusp of change: Persianate compositions and text panels, yet figures, textiles and faces drawn with a local hand—the distinct pre-Mughal Indo-Persian painting of Mandu.

i18n.hi: इन तस्वीरों में एक बदलती अस्लूब झलकती है: फ़ारसी अंदाज़ की जमावट और लिखाई, पर शक्लें, कपड़े और चेहरे स्थानीय हाथ के – मांडू की अलग, मुग़ल-पूर्व हिंदो-फ़ारसी निगारी।

panels.shot: medium shot of a cook demonstrating a dish to a circle of attendants, one of whom quietly takes notes on a small tablet
panels.action: In a kitchen courtyard, a cook in a simple turban stirs a pot thick with milk and spices as attendants watch intently, one kneeling to jot down ingredients and measures on a small waxed tablet.

dialogue.text: Across its folios, the Nimatnama records ways to prepare fish and meat, breads and sweets, preserves and pickles, capturing elite Malwa taste at a moment when Persian and Indian traditions were mingling in the pot.

i18n.hi: हर पन्ने पर निमत्नामा में मछली और गोश्त, रोटी और मिठाइयाँ, अचार और मुरब्बे दर्ज हैं – जब मालवा के इन्तिखाबी ज़ायके में फ़ारसी और हिंदुस्तानी रिवायतें एक ही देग में घुल रहीं थीं।

panels.shot: split-focus close-up: on one side a recipe text mentioning oils and herbs; on the other a miniature showing an attendant massaging a seated figure
panels.action: On the right, a miniature shows an attendant massaging the shoulders of a seated noble with a small flask beside them; on the left, the facing page bears lines of text describing oils, herbs and their effects on the body.

dialogue.text: It is not only a cookbook: the manuscript moves from kitchen to bathhouse and bedchamber, detailing perfumed oils, hair treatments, aphrodisiacs, digestive aids and cooling drinks as part of one continuous care of the body.

i18n.hi: ये सिर्फ़ रसोई की किताब नहीं: ये रसोई से हमाम और शयनकक्ष तक जाती है – सुगंधित तेल, बालों की देखभाल, मर्दानगी बढ़ाने के नुस्ख़े, हाज़मे की मदद और ठंडे शरबत – सब जिस्म की लगातार निगरानी का हिस्सा।

panels.shot: medium shot of Ghiyas-ud-din reclining as attendants bring him a spiced drink and betel leaves, with a tray of small jars nearby
panels.action: Ghiyas-ud-din reclines against bolsters in a shady loggia, accepting a spiced drink from one attendant while another offers folded betel leaves from a tray laden with jars of condiments and aromatic pastes.

dialogue.text: Firishta paints a picture of a ruler surrounded by women, musicians and foods, and the Nimatnama’s recipes for paan, sherbets and stimulating mixtures echo that reputation of a sovereign who ruled as much through delight as through decree.

i18n.hi: फिरिश्ता एक ऐसे बादशाह की तस्वीर उकेरता है जो औरतों, फ़नकारों और लज़्ज़तों से घिरा है; निमत्नामा के पान, शरबत और जोश बढ़ाने वाले नुस्ख़े उसी बादशाह की शोहरत दोहराते हैं, जो फ़रमान जितना ही लुत्फ़ से भी हुक्मरानी करता था।

panels.speaker: ghiyas_ud_din_khalji
panels.shot: close-up of Ghiyas-ud-din’s face in profile, eyes half-closed, as he smells a small vial of perfume
panels.action: In profile, Ghiyas-ud-din gently uncaps a tiny vial and lifts it to his nose, his eyes half-closed as he tests the perfume while light falls on the fine script of an open folio beside him.

dialogue.speaker: ghiyas_ud_din_khalji
dialogue.text: A ruler must know every scent of his house.

i18n.hi: हाकिम को अपने घर की हर ख़ुशबू पहचाननी चाहिए।

panels.shot: wide shot of women in the zenana kitchen area preparing food, some grinding spices, others rolling dough, while a eunuch overseer watches
panels.action: In a spacious inner-court kitchen, women grind spices on long stones, roll out flatbreads and stir pots, as a eunuch in fine garments stands at the doorway overseeing the bustling, smoke-filled scene.

dialogue.text: The manuscript hints at gendered labour in these pleasures: many recipes assume attendants and female cooks in the women’s quarters, their unseen hands sustaining the ordered abundance of the sultan’s table.

i18n.hi: पुस्तक में इन लज़्ज़तों के पीछे का औरतों का काम भी झलकता है: कई नुस्ख़े औरतों के महल में ख़ादिमों और बेग़मों की मौजूदगी मानते हैं, जिनके अदृश्य हाथों से सुल्तान की नेमतों से भरी मेज़ कायम रहती थी।

panels.shot: medium shot of a court physician examining an herb, with shelves of jars behind, and an open folio of Nimatnama on a stand
panels.action: A court physician lifts a sprig of herb to the light, shelves of labelled jars behind him, while beside his cushion an open folio shows lines of Persian prose and a small painting of a patient being examined.

dialogue.text: Alongside delicacies, the Nimatnama contains remedies for fevers, stomach pains and sexual weakness, part of an elite medical culture that saw diet, spice and regimen as instruments to tune the ruler’s body to rule.

i18n.hi: निमत्नामा में नाज़ुक पकवानों के साथ बुख़ार, पेट-दर्द और जिंसी कमज़ोरी के इलाज भी हैं – उस अशरफ़िया तबीयत-दानी का हिस्सा, जहाँ खाना, मसाला और परहेज़, बादशाह के जिस्म को हुकूमत के क़ाबिल रखने के औज़ार थे।

panels.shot: low-angle interior shot of a formal feast in a hall, with rows of guests and servants moving in disciplined lines bearing food
panels.action: In a grand hall lit by lamps, rows of guests sit on carpets before neat plates while servants move in disciplined lines, carrying steaming dishes of rice, meat and sweets on large platters held at shoulder height.

dialogue.text: To host such feasts was not frivolity alone: in a volatile Deccan, lavish banquets and the careful seating of allies, kin and rivals signalled hierarchy, favour and the sultan’s capacity to provide.

i18n.hi: ऐसी दावतें उड़ाना सिर्फ़ फ़िज़ूल-खर्ची नहीं था: बेचैन दक्कन में, धूमधाम से सजाए मेहफिलें और रिश्तेदारों, साथियों और दुश्मनों की नाप-तौल कर बैठकी, रुतबा, नेअमत और सुल्तान की क़ाबिल-ए-इनायत होने की निशानी थीं।

panels.shot: transition shot: the same workshop now under a different ruler’s emblem, scribes still at work but with some folios unfinished
panels.action: The familiar workshop appears again, but a different emblem hangs on the wall; scribes continue their work, yet some folios rest blank, others half-painted, as if the project is being nudged, altered, but not abandoned.

dialogue.text: As Ghiyas-ud-din’s reign ended and Nasir Shah’s began, the Nimatnama continued to grow, its attributions shifting, its pages hinting at continuity and change in patronage rather than a single author’s hand.

i18n.hi: जब ग़ियास-उद-दीन का दौर ख़त्म हुआ और नासिर शाह तख़्त पर आया, निमत्नामा बढ़ती रही – कुछ नुस्ख़ों की सँद खत बदलती, पन्नों पर एक ही सरपरस्ती में निरंतरता और बदलाव, दोनों के इशारे थे, ना कि सिर्फ़ एक लेखक का हाथ।

panels.shot: close shot of a later marginal note or ownership mark on the manuscript, the page slightly worn, hinting at its later journeys
panels.action: A worn page of the manuscript shows a small later note and an ownership stamp in the margin, the edges darkened by use, suggesting that the book has passed through many hands beyond Mandu’s palaces.

dialogue.text: Over centuries, this single volume travelled far from its kitchens of origin, eventually entering the British Library as IO Islamic MS 149, one fragment of Malwa’s courtly life preserved in paper and paint.

i18n.hi: सदियों में ये एक किताब, अपनी मांडू की रसोइयों से बहुत दूर निकल गई, आख़िरकार ब्रिटिश लाइब्रेरी में ‘आईओ इस्लामिक एमएस 149’ बनकर दाख़िल हुई – मालवा की दरबारी ज़िंदगी का एक टुकड़ा, काग़ज़ और रंग में बचा हुआ।

panels.shot: wide shot of a modern reading room table with the Nimatnama open under soft light and gloved hands pointing, but no faces shown
panels.action: On a modern wooden table under soft museum lighting, the Nimatnama lies open in a cradle, gloved hands gently turning a folio as the painted scene of a medieval banquet glows against the quiet of the reading room.

dialogue.text: Today, historians and readers study its folios to glimpse not only recipes but hierarchies of service, ideals of beauty, techniques of healing and a visual language poised on the eve of the Mughal age.

i18n.hi: आज इतिहासकार और पाठक इसकी शीटें पढ़कर सिर्फ़ नुस्ख़े नहीं, बल्कि नौकरियों की सीढियाँ, खूबसूरती के आदर्श, इलाज के तरीक़े और मुग़ल दौर से ठीक पहले की तस्वीर-ज़ुबान की झलक तलाशते हैं।

panels.shot: final reflective shot: ghostly overlap of Ghiyas-ud-din in his terrace court over the modern open manuscript, blending past and present
panels.action: The image blends Ghiyas-ud-din once more on his terrace above Mandu, surrounded by trays and attendants, with the faint superimposed shape of the open Nimatnama folio, as if the court has been folded into the book itself.

dialogue.text: The Nimatnama reminds us that a court is remembered not only for battles or decrees, but for how it fed, perfumed and disciplined the body—and that a single recipe book can hold the texture of an entire world.

i18n.hi: निमत्नामा याद दिलाती है कि दरबार सिर्फ़ जंगों या फ़रमानों से नहीं, बल्कि खाने, खुश्बू और जिस्म की तरबियत से भी याद रखा जाता है – और ये कि एक रसोई की किताब भी पूरे ज़माने की बनावट समेट सकती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Where Mandu Wrote Its Hunger for Power in Ink and Spice
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ मांडू ने स्याही और मसाले से सत्ता की भूख लिखी
